claims.text: The self is a constant and unchangeable essence in man, beyond the limits of any change, described as pure subject-object-less consciousness, reality, and bliss.

claims.text: Consciousness stands in need of the aid of Nature in the completion of the production of its effect, Self-consciousness.

claims.text: The self, the pure cit, is neither illusory nor an abstraction; it is concrete but transcendent, giving unity to all the movements of the knowledge-composites of subtle stuff.

limitations: The supplied evidence only provides a limited understanding of the relationship between consciousness and the self in Samkhya.
summary: In Samkhya, consciousness is related to the self and experienced reality through the concept of pure subject-object-less consciousness, which is the inmost essence of a person, beyond any change.
unsupported_aspects: The exact nature of the relationship between consciousness and experienced reality in Samkhya is not fully supported by the supplied evidence.
